title: UNION ALL — Combine Multiple Sources
description: Combine orders from multiple years using UNION ALL to get a combined list.

data.text: Write a query that combines all orders from 2023 and 2024 into one result set, marking which year each order belongs to.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, TotalAmount, '2023' AS OrderYear
FROM Orders
WHERE YEAR(OrderDate) = 2023
UNION ALL
SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, TotalAmount, '2024' AS OrderYear
FROM Orders
WHERE YEAR(OrderDate) = 2024
ORDER BY OrderDate DESC;

data.title: Explanation
data.text: UNION ALL does NOT remove duplicates, so it is faster than UNION. Use it when you know the sources are distinct or when duplicates are acceptable. For combining partitioned data (e.g., by year), UNION ALL is the right choice.
